claims.explanation: WZ-4002 is a dual EGFR/ERBB2 kinase inhibitor, and the selectively killed lines are enriched for EGFR-mutant NSCLC (HCC4006, PC14) and other lines with activated RTK/RAS-MAPK signaling, whereas the least affected lines are dominated by KRAS-mutant or NF1-mutant tumors that bypass EGFR/ERBB2 dependence. The pattern suggests that sensitivity requires oncogenic dependence on EGFR/ERBB2 signaling, while downstream RAS-MAPK activation (KRAS, NF1, BRAF) confers resistance.

features.basis: EGFR-mutant NSCLC lines are among the most killed; EGFR is the primary drug target
ERBB2 is a direct drug target and ERBB2 mutations can be inhibitor-sensitive
KRAS-mutant lines (RERFLCAD1, SW1573, OV7, TCCPAN2) are among the least affected, indicating bypass of EGFR/ERBB2 dependence
NF1 loss activates RAS-MAPK downstream of EGFR/ERBB2; NF1-mutant lines are enriched among least affected
BRAF-mutant lines (OV90, LOXIMVI, G361, WM793, HT115) are largely in the least-affected group, suggesting downstream MAPK activation bypasses EGFR/ERBB2 inhibition
High EGFR expression would increase dependence on EGFR signaling and drug sensitivity
ERBB2 overexpression/amplification predicts response to ERBB2-targeting inhibitors
PTEN loss activates PI3K-AKT signaling downstream of RTKs; PTEN-mutant lines appear in both groups but may reduce dependence on EGFR/ERBB2
PIK3CA mutations activate PI3K downstream of EGFR/ERBB2 and may bypass receptor inhibition
TP53 mutation is common across lines and not selective; included only as a weak negative feature
